name: The Breathing Arch
region_detail: A rocky desert passage removed from the principal caravan roads.
site_type: rock formation | Natural wonders | Wind-carved sandstone arch and sheltered natural alcoves.
history: Centuries of erosion have shaped an immense arch above a narrow passage between sandstone outcrops. Qasari travelers have long recognized the formation as a landmark and shelter during strong winds. Small cavities in the rock produce different tones according to the direction and strength of the wind.
current_state: The arch remains a useful landmark for travelers following the lesser passage. Its sheltered alcoves contain traces of old campfires and inscriptions left by passing caravans. Wind occasionally carries the sounds of the cavities far across the surrounding plain.
inhabitants: Desert birds, lizards, and other wildlife; occasional travelers sheltering beneath the arch.
danger_level: Low in suitable weather; moderate during severe winds or rockfall.
points_of_interest:
Immense sandstone arch; resonant cavities; sheltered alcoves; weathered travelers’ inscriptions; old campfire sites; elevated view of the surrounding plain.

Unresolved elements: The age and meaning of the oldest inscriptions; Whether the formation’s unusual acoustics have ever been employed as signals; The suitability of the lesser passage for laden caravans.
discovery: A rocky desert passage removed from the principal caravan roads. Experienced Qasari guides recognize the arch and its characteristic sounds. Travelers crossing the rocky plain may notice it from a distance.
